structure:
repos/trade-imports-ins-tests on main at c433e6b (27 November 2026), the Playwright end-to-end, accessibility, visual and security suite for every trade imports service. One directory per domain under tests/: animals, ins, plants and animals-admin. The scope takes in tests/animals and tests/ins only; tests/plants and tests/animals-admin are left out, as are the plants and animals-admin page objects, flows and domain folders that only they use.

What moved since the last extract (26 November): EUDPA-776 retired the live-animals contact address coverage, deleting tests/animals/e2e/pages/contact-address.spec.ts and page-objects/animals/contact-address-page.ts and trimming the journey flow, seed steps, outbox and DB models, the address book specs on both sides, the a11y journey scans, the Dynamics data specs and the review visual baselines to match; EUDPA-832 added a country-name search to the animals party picker spec (addresses-picker.spec.ts) and its seed; EUDPA-827 proved the pickers page at eight and restate the chosen address; EUDPA-714 added an INS dashboard test that another organisation sees none of a notification; EUDPA-787 ran @ios tests on real iPhones and @cross-browser tests in branded Chrome on macOS through BrowserStack (fixtures/browserstack.ts, utils/playwright/shared-config.ts) and rewrote both cross-browser READMEs; EUDPA-802 reworked the paginated dashboard a11y scan, the axe exclusion for the file upload button and the conditional-pages security scan; EUDPA-696 (Design Release 2.1 overview and review) reshaped the overview, review, declaration, confirmation and notification view specs and page objects.

In scope by the numbers: tests/animals holds e2e/pages (20 specs and a README: one spec per live-animals journey page), e2e/features (60 files: a README, 45 flat specs, features/address-book with 9 specs, features/reference-lists with 5 specs), e2e/journeys (15 files: a README, 7 flat specs, journeys/dynamics with 3, journeys/persistence with 4), e2e/visual (12 specs, with committed PNG baselines beside them in *-snapshots folders for chromium-darwin and chromium-linux), a11y (12 specs and a README), security (8 frontend specs and 1 backend spec) and cross-browser (a README only, no specs: the cross-browser runs select tagged tests from the other folders). tests/ins holds e2e/features (36 files: address-book with 20 specs and 5 helpers, transporters with 4 specs and a runner, notification-type with 1 spec, and 5 flat specs for the INS dashboard navigation, page titles, cross-service sessions, organisation scoping and the aggregated notification), a11y (9 specs and a README), security/address-book (2 specs) and cross-browser (a README only). Several specs generate tests in a loop over a table, so the run-time count is higher than the literal test() count.

The suite keeps its support code outside tests/: page-objects/{animals,ins,ins/address-book,shared,shared/auth}, flows/{animals,ins,shared} (flows/animals/journey.ts drives most journeys), domain/{animals,ins,shared} (constants, expected copy, option lists and DB/API/Dynamics models), fixtures/ (the ui, auth-state, a11y, visual, security, seed-context and BrowserStack fixtures), utils/ (helpers, plus utils/playwright for the shared config and projects, utils/zap and utils/dynamics) and config/ (base URLs, timeouts, users, service tags, ZAP). Repo-level configuration and documentation sit at the root: playwright.config.ts (CDP target) and playwright.docker-compose.config.ts (local stack target); package.json's test scripts, which are how a domain and test type are selected; README.md (the per-domain and per-environment script and PROFILE tables); AGENTS.md; docs/{animals-journey,a11y,security,cross-browser}.md; .github/workflows; bin/ seeding and probe scripts; zap/ automation files. There is no rulings or decisions ledger in the repo: no spec/decisions.json and no decisions file outside node_modules, so the only rulings this source carries are the ones its docs and READMEs state in prose.

The committed PNG visual baselines are binary and are not read as text; the visual specs name them, and the part that owns those specs claims what each baseline is taken of and under what viewport and state, not the pixels.

Cut into 16 parts, the same slices as the 26 November extract so claim ids carry over: 11 over tests/animals (3 by journey page group, 3 by feature group, 1 for the animals-side address book, 1 for end-to-end journeys and reference lists, 1 for persistence and Dynamics, 1 for accessibility, 1 for visual and security), 4 over tests/ins (2 for the address book, 1 for the dashboard and notification type, 1 for transporters with INS accessibility and security) and 1 for the suite's own configuration, scripts and documentation. Page objects, flows, domain constants, fixtures and utils are read as full context by whichever parts' specs use them, and several parts therefore name the same support file; a claim comes from a test, so a support file read by two parts yields no duplicate claim.

parts.title: animals e2e/pages: live-animals question pages
parts.scope: The per-page specs for the live-animals journey's data-entry pages: origin of import, reason for import, consignment details, arrival details, commodity selection, animal identification, CPH number and additional details. Stops before the address, transited-countries and transporter pages (part 2) and before the review, declaration, confirmation, notification view and notification list pages (part 3).
covers: Every test in the 8 specs named in read, by its title: origin.spec.ts, import-reason.spec.ts, consignment-details.spec.ts, arrival-details.spec.ts, commodities.spec.ts, animal-identification.spec.ts, cph-number.spec.ts and additional-details.spec.ts, plus every test any of them generates by looping over a table of cases

For each of the 8 pages: the URL path the spec opens, the heading and caption it asserts, every field label, hint, option and legend quoted in the spec or in the page object and domain constants it asserts against, and whether the spec proves the field is required
Every validation rule the specs prove, with the error message verbatim and the error-summary wording

Every conditional branch the specs prove, such as the region-code reveal on origin of import, the purpose questions behind each reason for import, and the identifier panels the commodity choice reveals
What each page's Save and continue and Save and return to overview buttons are proven to do, and where each is proven to land
What the country-of-origin and port type-ahead are proven to do on these pages: the component used, its label and hint, and the announcements asserted
Any gap: a page in this group whose spec asserts nothing about a field, option or error the page object names

parts.title: animals e2e/pages: addresses, transited countries and transporters
parts.scope: The per-page specs for the live-animals journey's address, transited-countries and transporter pages: transited countries, the permanent address page, the party pickers and party edit form as these specs reach them, and the four transporter pages. The contact address page and its spec were removed from the suite on 25 November 2026 (EUDPA-776), so no contact address spec belongs to any part. Stops at the specs in tests/animals/e2e/features/address-book (part 7), which cover the address book hand-off rather than the pages themselves.
covers: Every test in the 7 specs named in read, by its title: transited-countries.spec.ts, permanent-address.spec.ts, private-transporter.spec.ts, commercial-transporter.spec.ts, transporter.spec.ts, transporter-add.spec.ts and transporter-add-save-cancel.spec.ts
The transited-countries page: the Add country button, the table of added countries, the remove action, the empty state, and what the specs prove about adding, removing and ordering

The permanent address page: every field label, hint and option, every validation message verbatim, which commodities the specs prove reach it, and what the specs prove about the country list and the manual-entry route
The party pickers: the page size the specs assert, the radio or link rows, the 'Selected address' restatement if asserted, the Add a new address link, and the Change and Remove actions

The four transporter pages: the private-or-commercial type question with its options and hints, the private transporter's country field, the commercial transporter's forced country, every validation message verbatim, and what Save and Cancel are proven to do on the add page
Any gap: a field, option or error named in the page objects or domain constants in read that no test in this part asserts
That the live-animals journey no longer has a contact address page: what the remaining specs and flows/animals/journey.ts walk in its place, as the specs show it

parts.title: animals e2e: overview, review, declaration, confirmation, notification view and notification list
parts.scope: The specs for the pages at the end of and around the live-animals journey: declaration, confirmation, the notification view in each state, the animals notification list and its pagination, plus the two list feature specs for sort and search. Stops at amend, cancel amend and delete, which part 6 owns, and at the a11y and visual views of these same pages, which parts 10 and 11 own.
covers: Every test in the 7 specs named in read, by its title: declaration.spec.ts, confirmation.spec.ts, notification-view-states.spec.ts, notification-dashboard.spec.ts, notification-dashboard-pagination.spec.ts, notification-dashboard-sort.spec.ts, notification-dashboard-search.spec.ts
The declaration page: its heading, the declaration wording quoted, the checkbox or statement, the submit button and every validation message verbatim
The confirmation page: the panel wording, the reference shown, every what-happens-next item and every link off it

The notification view: every state the spec drives it into (draft, submitted, amending, cancelled, deleted and any other), and for each the status tag text, the header buttons and which form each posts, the summary rows and the warnings or banners shown

The animals notification list: the column headings, the row content, the status tags, the empty state, the page size and pagination wording, every sort option and its order, and what the search box is proven to match
Any gap: a state, column or action the page objects name that no test in this part drives

parts.title: animals e2e/features: journey scope, conditional rules and overview navigation
parts.scope: The 20 flat feature specs that prove which questions the live-animals journey asks for which answers, and how a user moves between the overview, the question pages and check your answers. Stops at the document specs (part 5) and the amend, delete and auth specs (part 6).
covers: Every test in the 20 specs named in read, by its title, including every test generated by looping over a table of commodity or answer cases

Each scope rule the suite proves, as a rule: which commodity codes or answers make the CPH number, number of packages, additional details, transit means, reason-and-purpose, private transporter and commercial transporter questions appear, and which make them skipped
The animal identifier rules: which identifier panels each commodity choice reveals, the cap on identifiers and the error message when it is exceeded, verbatim
The arrival-date window: the rule, the boundary the spec drives and the error message verbatim
The overview task list: every hub group and task row name proven, each row's status wording, and the check-your-answers rows each group maps to
The Change links from check your answers: where each lands, what is prefilled and where returning lands
Save and return to overview: the checks it is proven to make on each page and where it lands
The reference strip and page header content proven on every journey page, and the headers and page titles the specs assert
What the port-of-entry select and country-of-origin type-ahead are proven to do: component, keyboard behaviour, no-results wording and announcements
Any gap: a scope rule or hub group the constants in read name that no test asserts

parts.title: animals e2e/features: accompanying documents and promoted notifications
parts.scope: The 11 flat feature specs for the accompanying-documents feature and for a promoted notification's documents and lifecycle: entry, upload, save buttons, limits, rejection, virus scanning, two tabs, the back button, refresh without JavaScript and large uploads. Stops at the amend and delete specs (part 6).

The documents page: its heading, the document type question with every option and hint, the file input and its hint, the add and remove actions, the table or list of added documents and every column in it
Every validation and refusal message the specs prove verbatim: no file chosen, no type chosen, a rejected file type, a file over the size limit, a file a byte over it, and the count limit
The virus-scan lifecycle: each status the specs drive and the wording shown for it, including what a user sees while a scan is pending and what happens when a scan fails
What each save button on the documents page is proven to do and where it lands
What the suite proves about the no-JavaScript path: a refresh after an upload, the back button, and two tabs uploading over each other
What a promoted (submitted) notification's documents are proven to allow and refuse, and the lifecycle states promoted-lifecycle.spec.ts drives
Any gap: a document type, limit or status named in the constants and helpers in read that no test asserts

parts.title: animals e2e/features: amend, cancel amend, delete, stale submit, auth and organisation scoping

The amend journey: how it starts, what the review and its title read during an amend, every way an amend is proven to end, and what each ending leaves the notification in
The cancel amend page: its heading, its wording, its buttons, what cancelling is proven to restore, and whether it is a page or a dialog
The delete confirmation page: its heading, its wording, its buttons, what deleting is proven to do and where it lands
Declaring a notification whose answers have gone stale: what the user is shown and what the suite proves must happen

The consignment addresses page: its heading and section heading as asserted, every party row, each row's Change, Add and Remove actions, and the incomplete-card or validation wording verbatim

parts.title: animals e2e: whole journeys and reference-list content
parts.scope: The 7 flat specs under tests/animals/e2e/journeys that walk a whole live-animals journey, together with the 5 specs under tests/animals/e2e/features/reference-lists that prove what each reference list serves. Stops at journeys/dynamics and journeys/persistence, which part 9 owns.
covers: Every test in the 12 specs named in read, by its title: save-and-continue.spec.ts, back.spec.ts, back-entry-points.spec.ts, pet-cats-air-permanent-address.spec.ts, horse-temporary-admission.spec.ts, poultry-rail-transit.spec.ts, promoted-notification.spec.ts, and the 5 reference-list specs

Each whole journey the suite walks, as an ordered list of pages with the answer given at each: the pet-cats-by-air journey with a permanent address, the horse temporary-admission journey, the poultry rail-transit journey and the promoted-notification journey

parts.title: animals e2e/journeys: what is stored and what is published
parts.scope: The 4 specs under tests/animals/e2e/journeys/persistence and the 3 under tests/animals/e2e/journeys/dynamics, with the DB, API and Dynamics models they assert against: what a notification, its commodity lines and its accompanying documents hold once stored, what the API seed produces compared with the UI, and what is published to Dynamics. The only part that claims the models under domain/animals/models and domain/ins/models.

Every field of the stored notification document, its commodity lines, its accompanying documents and the outbox event that the specs or the models in read name, with the shape and type each holds
The parity rule the API seed is held to: which fields a seeded notification must match a UI-entered one on, and where the suite allows them to differ
What is published to Dynamics: each field of the importer notification, each event the suite proves is published, the order and the gaps the data-gaps spec names as allowed
The aggregated notification document and the address document shapes the INS read model is held to
Any security finding, stated in general terms only: name the area, never how to exploit it

parts.title: animals a11y: the accessibility suite
parts.scope: The 12 specs under tests/animals/a11y and the a11y fixture and helpers: which pages and states are scanned, at which viewports, with which rules and which exclusions. Does not cover the INS a11y specs, which part 15 owns.
covers: Every test in the 12 specs named in read, by its title, including every test generated by looping over a list of pages or viewports

Every page and state the suite scans, named: each journey page in its initial, filled and error state, each conditional page, the notification list views, the notification view states, the lifecycle states, the address edit page and sign-in
Every viewport the suite scans at, with its size
The rule set and standard the scans are run against, and every exclusion or allowed violation with the reason given for it
What a11y-scan-detects-violations.spec.ts proves about the scanner itself
Any gap: a page the journey specs walk that no a11y scan covers

parts.title: animals visual and security suites
parts.scope: The 12 visual-regression specs under tests/animals/e2e/visual with their committed PNG baselines, and the 8 frontend security specs under tests/animals/security with the ZAP configuration. The backend security spec is part 9's, with the models it asserts.
covers: Every test in the 20 specs named in read, by its title: the 12 visual specs and the 8 frontend security specs

For each visual spec: the page and state it photographs, the viewport, what is masked or frozen to make the shot stable, and the baseline file names it compares against (named, not read as pixels) — including that each baseline exists for both chromium-darwin and chromium-linux

The components the visual suite pins: the identification card, the party-picker search row, the date picker at rest, on hover, on focus and open by mouse and by keyboard, the overview totals, the review and the refused review at desktop and phone, and the declaration
For each security spec: the journey or page it walks for the scan, and the contexts it puts in scope
The ZAP set-up as rules: the contexts, the alert thresholds, every suppressed or ignored rule with the reason, and the no-traffic gate
Any weakness found, stated in general terms only: name the area, never how to exploit it
Any gap: a page the visual or security suite does not reach that docs/security.md or the specs imply it should

parts.title: ins address book: the list, its tabs, filters and roles

The country list the address book offers: its source, the entries asserted and the order

parts.title: The suite's configuration, scripts and documentation
parts.scope: The repo's own shared configuration and prose, which say what is run where and what the suite claims to prove: the two Playwright configs, the test scripts, the service base URLs and tags, the CI workflows, and every root and docs markdown file. No tests/animals or tests/ins spec belongs to this part.
